tex_content.html:
Theorem
[Interior Hessian Hölder estimate in dimension two] 1. ch17:17.9\group chapter-17Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0463 Let $u\in C^3(\Omega )$ solve $F[u]=0$ in $\Omega \subset \mathbb R^2$. Assume $F\in C^1(\Gamma )$ is elliptic with respect to $u$ and satisfies (17.24). For every $\Omega '\Subset \Omega $, \begin{equation} \tag {17.25} [D^2u]_{\alpha ;\Omega '}\le \frac{C}{d^\alpha } \bigl(|D^2u|_{0;\Omega }+\mu d(1+|Du|_{1;\Omega })\bigr), \end{equation} where $d=\operatorname {dist}(\Omega ',\partial \Omega )$ and $C,\alpha $ depend only on $\Lambda /\lambda $.
Proof

\sketch Each $D_ku$ satisfies the linear uniformly elliptic equation (17.23). The two-dimensional Hölder gradient estimate for that equation, applied on balls of radius comparable to $d$, gives (17.25).

□
